TITLE: Pattern Server - REST API
DESCRIPTION: HTTP server providing programmatic access to Effect patterns with proper error handling and validation.

SOURCE: https://github.com/pauljphilp/effectpatterns/blob/main/context7.md

## Pattern Server - REST API

### Description

HTTP server providing programmatic access to Effect patterns with proper error handling and validation.

### Starting the Server

```bash
bun run server:dev
```

### Endpoints

#### Health Check

##### Method
GET

##### Endpoint
`/health`

##### Description
Checks the health status of the server.

##### Response Example (200)

```json
{
  "status": "ok"
}
```

#### Get All Rules

##### Method
GET

##### Endpoint
`/api/v1/rules`

##### Description
Retrieves a list of all available rules.

##### Response Example (200)

```json
[
  {
    "id": "combinator-map",
    "title": "Transforming Values with map",
    "description": "Use map to transform results...",
    "skillLevel": "beginner",
    "useCase": ["Combinators", "Composition"],
    "content": "# Transforming Values with `map`\n\n..."
  }
]
```

#### Get Single Rule by ID

##### Method
GET

##### Endpoint
`/api/v1/rules/:id`

##### Parameters

*   **Path Parameters**
    *   `id` (string) - Required - The unique identifier of the rule.

##### Description
Retrieves a specific rule by its ID.

##### Response Example (200)

```json
{
  "id": "combinator-map",
  "title": "Transforming Values with map",
  "description": "Use map to transform results...",
  "skillLevel": "beginner",
  "useCase": ["Combinators", "Composition"],
  "content": "# Transforming Values with `map`\n\n..."
}
```

##### Response Example (404 Not Found)

```json
{
  "error": "Rule not found"
}
```

### Error Handling

The server returns specific error messages for different error conditions, such as a rule not being found. The example below shows a 404 response for a non-existent rule.

```bash
curl http://localhost:3001/api/v1/rules/nonexistent
```

**Response:**

```json
{
  "error": "Rule not found"
}
```

**Status:** `404`
```

TITLE: Handle Errors and Provide Fallbacks with effect-ts
DESCRIPTION: Demonstrates how to recover from failures, provide default values for Options, and handle Left values in Either. It covers catching all errors in Effects, using orElse for Options and Either, and pattern matching on Effect results.

SOURCE: https://github.com/pauljphilp/effectpatterns/blob/main/rules/by-use-case/composition.md

LANGUAGE: typescript
CODE:
```
import { Effect, Option, Either } from "effect";

// Effect: Recover from any error
const effect = Effect.fail("fail!").pipe(
  Effect.catchAll((err) => Effect.succeed(`Recovered from: ${err}`))
); // Effect<string>

// Option: Provide a fallback if value is None
const option = Option.none().pipe(
  Option.orElse(() => Option.some("default"))
); // Option<string>

// Either: Provide a fallback if value is Left
const either = Either.left("error").pipe(
  Either.orElse(() => Either.right("fallback"))
); // Either<never, string>

// Effect: Pattern match on success or failure
const matchEffect = Effect.fail("fail!").pipe(
  Effect.match({
    onFailure: (err) => `Error: ${err}`,
    onSuccess: (value) => `Success: ${value}`,
  })
); // Effect<string>
```

import { SqlClient } from "@effect/sql"

const RepoVisibilitySchema = Schema.Literal("public", "private", "internal")

export type RepoVisibility = Schema.Type<typeof RepoVisibilitySchema>

const RepoSchema = Schema.Struct({
  id: Schema.Number,
  githubRepoId: Schema.optional(Schema.Number),
  owner: Schema.NonEmptyString,
  name: Schema.NonEmptyString,
  fullName: Schema.NonEmptyString,
  visibility: RepoVisibilitySchema,
  isActive: Schema.Boolean,
  backfilledAt: Schema.optional(Schema.Date),
  createdAt: Schema.Date,
  updatedAt: Schema.Date
})

export type Repo = Schema.Type<typeof RepoSchema>

const UpsertInputSchema = Schema.Struct({
  owner: Schema.NonEmptyString,
  name: Schema.NonEmptyString,
  visibility: RepoVisibilitySchema,
  githubRepoId: Schema.optional(Schema.Number)
})

export type UpsertInput = Schema.Type<typeof UpsertInputSchema>

interface RepoRow {
  readonly id: number | string
  readonly githubRepoId: number | string | null
  readonly owner: string
  readonly name: string
  readonly fullName: string
  readonly visibility: RepoVisibility
  readonly isActive: boolean
  readonly backfilledAt: string | Date | null
  readonly createdAt: string | Date
  readonly updatedAt: string | Date
}

const decodeRepo = Schema.decodeUnknown(RepoSchema)
const decodeUpsertInput = Schema.decodeUnknown(UpsertInputSchema)

const toRepo = (row: RepoRow) =>
  decodeRepo({
    id: typeof row.id === "string" ? Number.parseInt(row.id, 10) : row.id,
    githubRepoId:
      row.githubRepoId === null
        ? undefined
        : typeof row.githubRepoId === "string"
          ? Number.parseInt(row.githubRepoId, 10)
          : row.githubRepoId,
    owner: row.owner,
    name: row.name,
    fullName: row.fullName,
    visibility: row.visibility,
    isActive: row.isActive,
    backfilledAt:
      row.backfilledAt === null
        ? undefined
        : row.backfilledAt instanceof Date
          ? row.backfilledAt
          : new Date(row.backfilledAt),
    createdAt: row.createdAt instanceof Date ? row.createdAt : new Date(row.createdAt),
    updatedAt: row.updatedAt instanceof Date ? row.updatedAt : new Date(row.updatedAt)
  }).pipe(Effect.mapError((error) => new Error(String(error))))

const selectProjection = `
  id,
  github_repo_id AS "githubRepoId",
  owner,
  name,
  full_name AS "fullName",
  visibility,
  is_active AS "isActive",
  backfilled_at AS "backfilledAt",
  created_at AS "createdAt",
  updated_at AS "updatedAt"
`

const makeLive = Effect.gen(function* () {
  const sql = yield* SqlClient.SqlClient

  const upsert = (input: UpsertInput) =>
    decodeUpsertInput(input).pipe(
      Effect.mapError((error) => new Error(String(error))),
      Effect.flatMap((validated) =>
        sql<RepoRow>`
          INSERT INTO repos (github_repo_id, owner, name, visibility)
          VALUES (${validated.githubRepoId ?? null}, ${validated.owner}, ${validated.name}, ${validated.visibility})
          ON CONFLICT (owner, name) DO UPDATE SET
            github_repo_id = EXCLUDED.github_repo_id,
            visibility = EXCLUDED.visibility
          RETURNING ${sql.unsafe(selectProjection)}
        `.pipe(
          Effect.flatMap((rows) =>
            rows.length === 0
              ? Effect.fail(new Error("Failed to upsert repo"))
              : toRepo(rows[0])
          )
        )
      )
    )

  const listActive = sql<RepoRow>`
    SELECT ${sql.unsafe(selectProjection)}
    FROM repos
    WHERE is_active = TRUE
    ORDER BY owner, name
  `.pipe(
    Effect.flatMap((rows) => Effect.forEach(rows, toRepo, { concurrency: 1 })),
    Effect.map((rows) => rows as ReadonlyArray<Repo>)
  )

  return {
    upsert,
    listActive
  } as const
})

export class ReposStore extends Context.Tag("ci-dashboard/ReposStore")<
  ReposStore,
  {
    readonly upsert: (input: UpsertInput) => Effect.Effect<Repo>
    readonly listActive: Effect.Effect<ReadonlyArray<Repo>>
  }
>() {}

export const Live = Layer.effect(ReposStore, makeLive)

export const upsert = (input: UpsertInput) =>
  Effect.flatMap(ReposStore, (store) => store.upsert(input))

export const listActive = Effect.flatMap(ReposStore, (store) => store.listActive)"}

})

  head_sha AS "headSha",

  run_started_at AS "runStartedAt",
  run_completed_at AS "runCompletedAt",
  ingested_at AS "ingestedAt",
  ingested_updated_at AS "ingestedUpdatedAt"
`

const normalizeQuery = (input: QueryInput | undefined) =>
  decodeQueryInput(input ?? {}).pipe(
    Effect.map((parsed) => ({
      ...parsed,
      limit: Math.min(Math.max(parsed.limit ?? DEFAULT_QUERY_LIMIT, 1), MAX_QUERY_LIMIT)

    Effect.mapError((error) => new Error(String(error)))
  )

const makeLive = Effect.gen(function* () {
  const sql = yield* SqlClient.SqlClient

  const upsert = (input: UpsertInput) =>
    decodeUpsertInput(input).pipe(
      Effect.mapError((error) => new Error(String(error))),
      Effect.flatMap((validated) =>
        sql<RunRow>`
          INSERT INTO runs (
            repo_id,
            repo_full_name,
            github_run_id,
            github_run_number,
            github_run_attempt,
            workflow_name,
            workflow_id,
            display_title,
            event,
            status,
            conclusion,
            head_branch,
            head_sha,
            html_url,
            actor_login,
            created_at,
            updated_at,
            run_started_at,
            run_completed_at
          )
          VALUES (
            ${validated.repoId},
            ${validated.repoFullName},
            ${validated.githubRunId},
            ${validated.githubRunNumber ?? null},
            ${validated.githubRunAttempt ?? null},
            ${validated.workflowName},
            ${validated.workflowId ?? null},
            ${validated.displayTitle ?? null},
            ${validated.event},
            ${validated.status},
            ${validated.conclusion ?? null},
            ${validated.headBranch ?? null},

            ${validated.createdAt},
            ${validated.updatedAt},
            ${validated.runStartedAt ?? null},
            ${validated.runCompletedAt ?? null}
          )

            github_run_number = EXCLUDED.github_run_number,
            github_run_attempt = EXCLUDED.github_run_attempt,

            workflow_id = EXCLUDED.workflow_id,

            event = EXCLUDED.event,
            status = EXCLUDED.status,
            conclusion = EXCLUDED.conclusion,

            head_sha = EXCLUDED.head_sha,

            actor_login = EXCLUDED.actor_login,
            created_at = EXCLUDED.created_at,
            updated_at = EXCLUDED.updated_at,
            run_started_at = EXCLUDED.run_started_at,
            run_completed_at = EXCLUDED.run_completed_at
          RETURNING ${sql.unsafe(selectProjection)}
        `.pipe(
          Effect.flatMap((rows) =>
            rows.length === 0 ? Effect.fail(new Error("Failed to upsert run")) : toRun(rows[0])
          )
        )
      )
    )

  const query = (input?: QueryInput) =>
    normalizeQuery(input).pipe(
      Effect.flatMap((filters) => {
        const whereClauses: Array<string | ReturnType<typeof sql.literal>> = []

        if (filters.repoFullName) {
          whereClauses.push(sql`repo_full_name = ${filters.repoFullName}`)
        }

        if (filters.status) {
          whereClauses.push(sql`status = ${filters.status}`)
        }

        if (filters.from) {
          whereClauses.push(sql`created_at >= ${filters.from}`)
        }

        }

          const pattern = `%${filters.search}%`
          whereClauses.push(
            sql`(
              workflow_name ILIKE ${pattern} OR
              head_branch ILIKE ${pattern} OR
              head_sha ILIKE ${pattern}
            )`
          )
        }

        if (filters.cursor) {
          whereClauses.push(
            sql`(created_at, github_run_id) < (${filters.cursor.createdAt}, ${filters.cursor.githubRunId})`
          )
        }

        const statement = whereClauses.length > 0
          ? sql<RunRow>`
              SELECT ${sql.unsafe(selectProjection)}
              FROM runs
              WHERE ${sql.and(whereClauses)}
              ORDER BY created_at DESC, github_run_id DESC
              LIMIT ${filters.limit}
            `

              SELECT ${sql.unsafe(selectProjection)}
              FROM runs
              ORDER BY created_at DESC, github_run_id DESC
              LIMIT ${filters.limit}
            `

    upsert,
    query

  }
>() {}

  Effect.flatMap(RunsStore, (store) => store.upsert(input))

export const query = (input?: QueryInput) =>
  Effect.flatMap(RunsStore, (store) => store.query(input))"}

Leaning on Effect Patterns, the strongest fit for our current DB work is the **“Map Database Errors to RepositoryError”** pattern from `/pauljphilp/effectpatterns` (see `content/published/mapping-errors-to-fit-your-domain.mdx`). It wraps low-level SQL failures and connection issues in a domain-specific error so repositories expose a clean, consistent error surface.

Why it matters here:
- Our stores (e.g. `packages/server/src/db/schema/repos.ts:73` and `packages/server/src/db/schema/runs.ts:154`) currently collapse validation/SQL problems into plain `Error(String(error))`, which hides whether the fault came from decoding, constraint conflicts, or connectivity.
- S‑014 will extend the same boundary for `JobsStore.upsertById`; introducing a `JobsRepositoryError` (mirroring `RepositoryError` in the pattern) keeps each store’s public API stable while letting callers recover intelligently.
- The pattern composes nicely with the schema-based validation we already use: decode failures stay tagged, and true SQL issues become a known repository error.

Suggested next steps:
1. Introduce a shared domain error (e.g. `DbRepositoryError`) and follow the pattern when mapping `Schema.decode` or `SqlClient` failures.
2. Update existing stores to return the new error type so the Jobs work inherits the safer boundary.
3. (Optional) add minimal tests hitting failure paths to prove the new error mapping behaves as expected.

{"result":"import { Duration, Effect, Layer, Redacted } from "effect"
import { PgClient } from "@effect/sql-pg"
import { SqlClient } from "@effect/sql"
import { Config } from "../config/Config"

const DEFAULT_MAX_CONNECTIONS = 10

const makeLayer = Effect.gen(function* () {
  const { databaseUrl } = yield* Config

  const layer = PgClient.layer({
    url: Redacted.make(databaseUrl),
    maxConnections: DEFAULT_MAX_CONNECTIONS,
    connectTimeout: Duration.seconds(10),
    idleTimeout: Duration.seconds(30),
    applicationName: "ci-dashboard"
  })

  yield* SqlClient.SqlClient.pipe(
    Effect.flatMap((client) => client`SELECT 1 as ok`),
    Effect.asUnit,
    Effect.annotateLogs({ component: "db" }),
    Effect.tap(() => Effect.logInfo("database connectivity verified")),
    Effect.tapErrorCause((cause) => Effect.logError(cause)),
    Effect.scoped,
    Effect.provideLayer(layer)
  )

  return layer
})

export const Live = Layer.unwrapEffect(makeLayer)

export const DbClient = SqlClient.SqlClient

export const sql = <A = unknown>(strings: TemplateStringsArray, ...values: Array<unknown>) =>
  Effect.flatMap(DbClient, (client) => client<A>(strings, ...values))"}

{"result":"import { Context, Effect, Layer, Schema } from "effect"
import { SqlClient } from "@effect/sql"

const JobStatusSchema = Schema.Literal("queued", "in_progress", "completed")

const JobConclusionSchema = Schema.Literal(
  "action_required",
  "cancelled",
  "failure",
  "neutral",
  "success",
  "skipped",
  "stale",
  "timed_out",
  "startup_failure"
)

export type JobStatus = Schema.Type<typeof JobStatusSchema>
export type JobConclusion = Schema.Type<typeof JobConclusionSchema>

const JobStepSchema = Schema.Struct({
  name: Schema.optional(Schema.String),
  status: JobStatusSchema,
  conclusion: Schema.optional(JobConclusionSchema),
  number: Schema.optional(Schema.Number),
  startedAt: Schema.optional(Schema.Date),
  completedAt: Schema.optional(Schema.Date)
})

export type JobStep = Schema.Type<typeof JobStepSchema>

const JobSchema = Schema.Struct({
  id: Schema.Number,
  runId: Schema.Number,
  githubJobId: Schema.Number,
  githubRunId: Schema.Number,
  githubRunAttempt: Schema.optional(Schema.Number),
  name: Schema.NonEmptyString,
  status: JobStatusSchema,
  conclusion: Schema.optional(JobConclusionSchema),
  startedAt: Schema.optional(Schema.Date),
  completedAt: Schema.optional(Schema.Date),
  queuedAt: Schema.optional(Schema.Date),
  htmlUrl: Schema.optional(Schema.String),
  checkRunUrl: Schema.optional(Schema.String),
  runnerName: Schema.optional(Schema.String),
  runnerGroup: Schema.optional(Schema.String),
  runnerId: Schema.optional(Schema.Number),
  labels: Schema.ReadonlyArray(Schema.String),
  steps: Schema.ReadonlyArray(JobStepSchema),
  createdAt: Schema.Date,
  updatedAt: Schema.Date
})

export type Job = Schema.Type<typeof JobSchema>

const UpsertInputSchema = Schema.Struct({
  runId: Schema.Number,
  githubJobId: Schema.Number,
  githubRunId: Schema.Number,
  githubRunAttempt: Schema.optional(Schema.Number),
  name: Schema.NonEmptyString,
  status: JobStatusSchema,
  conclusion: Schema.optional(JobConclusionSchema),
  startedAt: Schema.optional(Schema.Date),
  completedAt: Schema.optional(Schema.Date),
  queuedAt: Schema.optional(Schema.Date),
  htmlUrl: Schema.optional(Schema.String),
  checkRunUrl: Schema.optional(Schema.String),
  runnerName: Schema.optional(Schema.String),
  runnerGroup: Schema.optional(Schema.String),
  runnerId: Schema.optional(Schema.Number),
  labels: Schema.optional(Schema.Array(Schema.String)),
  steps: Schema.optional(Schema.Array(JobStepSchema))
})

export type UpsertInput = Schema.Type<typeof UpsertInputSchema>

interface JobRow {
  readonly id: number | string
  readonly runId: number | string
  readonly githubJobId: number | string
  readonly githubRunId: number | string
  readonly githubRunAttempt: number | string | null
  readonly name: string
  readonly status: JobStatus
  readonly conclusion: JobConclusion | null
  readonly startedAt: string | Date | null
  readonly completedAt: string | Date | null
  readonly queuedAt: string | Date | null
  readonly htmlUrl: string | null
  readonly checkRunUrl: string | null
  readonly runnerName: string | null
  readonly runnerGroup: string | null
  readonly runnerId: number | string | null
  readonly labels: ReadonlyArray<string> | null
  readonly steps: ReadonlyArray<unknown> | null
  readonly createdAt: string | Date
  readonly updatedAt: string | Date
}

const decodeJob = Schema.decodeUnknown(JobSchema)
const decodeUpsertInput = Schema.decodeUnknown(UpsertInputSchema)

const toNumber = (value: number | string) =>
  typeof value === "string" ? Number.parseInt(value, 10) : value

const toOptionalNumber = (value: number | string | null | undefined) =>
  value == null ? undefined : toNumber(value)

const toDate = (value: string | Date) => (value instanceof Date ? value : new Date(value))

const toOptionalDate = (value: string | Date | null | undefined) =>
  value == null ? undefined : toDate(value)

const toOptionalString = (value: string | null | undefined) => (value == null ? undefined : value)

const toSteps = (value: ReadonlyArray<unknown> | null | undefined) => {
  if (!Array.isArray(value)) {
    return Effect.succeed([] as ReadonlyArray<JobStep>)
  }

  const normalized = value.flatMap((step) => {
    if (step && typeof step === "object") {
      const candidate = step as Record<string, unknown>

      const startedAt = candidate.startedAt ?? candidate.started_at
      const completedAt = candidate.completedAt ?? candidate.completed_at

      return [
        {
          name: candidate.name ?? undefined,
          status: candidate.status,
          conclusion: candidate.conclusion ?? undefined,
          number: candidate.number ?? undefined,
          startedAt:
            startedAt == null
              ? undefined
              : startedAt instanceof Date
                ? startedAt
                : new Date(String(startedAt)),
          completedAt:
            completedAt == null
              ? undefined
              : completedAt instanceof Date
                ? completedAt
                : new Date(String(completedAt))
        }
      ]
    }

    return [] as ReadonlyArray<JobStep>
  })

  return Schema.decodeUnknown(Schema.Array(JobStepSchema))(normalized).pipe(
    Effect.mapError((error) => new Error(String(error)))
  )
}

const toJob = (row: JobRow) =>
  Effect.flatMap(
    toSteps(row.steps),
    (steps) =>
      decodeJob({
        id: toNumber(row.id),
        runId: toNumber(row.runId),
        githubJobId: toNumber(row.githubJobId),
        githubRunId: toNumber(row.githubRunId),
        githubRunAttempt: toOptionalNumber(row.githubRunAttempt),
        name: row.name,
        status: row.status,
        conclusion: row.conclusion ?? undefined,
        startedAt: toOptionalDate(row.startedAt),
        completedAt: toOptionalDate(row.completedAt),
        queuedAt: toOptionalDate(row.queuedAt),
        htmlUrl: toOptionalString(row.htmlUrl),
        checkRunUrl: toOptionalString(row.checkRunUrl),
        runnerName: toOptionalString(row.runnerName),
        runnerGroup: toOptionalString(row.runnerGroup),
        runnerId: toOptionalNumber(row.runnerId),
        labels: row.labels ?? [],
        steps,
        createdAt: toDate(row.createdAt),
        updatedAt: toDate(row.updatedAt)
      })
  ).pipe(Effect.mapError((error) => new Error(String(error))))

const selectProjection = `
  id,
  run_id AS "runId",
  github_job_id AS "githubJobId",
  github_run_id AS "githubRunId",
  github_run_attempt AS "githubRunAttempt",
  name,
  status,
  conclusion,
  started_at AS "startedAt",
  completed_at AS "completedAt",
  queued_at AS "queuedAt",
  html_url AS "htmlUrl",
  check_run_url AS "checkRunUrl",
  runner_name AS "runnerName",
  runner_group AS "runnerGroup",
  runner_id AS "runnerId",
  labels,
  steps,
  created_at AS "createdAt",
  updated_at AS "updatedAt"
`

const makeLive = Effect.gen(function* () {
  const sql = yield* SqlClient.SqlClient

  const upsertById = (input: UpsertInput) =>
    decodeUpsertInput(input).pipe(
      Effect.mapError((error) => new Error(String(error))),
      Effect.flatMap((validated) =>
        sql<JobRow>`
          INSERT INTO jobs (
            run_id,
            github_job_id,
            github_run_id,
            github_run_attempt,
            name,
            status,
            conclusion,
            started_at,
            completed_at,
            queued_at,
            html_url,
            check_run_url,
            runner_name,
            runner_group,
            runner_id,
            labels,
            steps
          )
          VALUES (
            ${validated.runId},
            ${validated.githubJobId},
            ${validated.githubRunId},
            ${validated.githubRunAttempt ?? null},
            ${validated.name},
            ${validated.status},
            ${validated.conclusion ?? null},
            ${validated.startedAt ?? null},
            ${validated.completedAt ?? null},
            ${validated.queuedAt ?? null},
            ${validated.htmlUrl ?? null},
            ${validated.checkRunUrl ?? null},
            ${validated.runnerName ?? null},
            ${validated.runnerGroup ?? null},
            ${validated.runnerId ?? null},
            ${validated.labels ?? []},
            ${validated.steps ?? []}
          )
          ON CONFLICT (github_job_id) DO UPDATE SET
            run_id = EXCLUDED.run_id,
            github_run_id = EXCLUDED.github_run_id,
            github_run_attempt = EXCLUDED.github_run_attempt,
            name = EXCLUDED.name,
            status = EXCLUDED.status,
            conclusion = EXCLUDED.conclusion,
            started_at = EXCLUDED.started_at,
            completed_at = EXCLUDED.completed_at,
            queued_at = EXCLUDED.queued_at,
            html_url = EXCLUDED.html_url,
            check_run_url = EXCLUDED.check_run_url,
            runner_name = EXCLUDED.runner_name,
            runner_group = EXCLUDED.runner_group,
            runner_id = EXCLUDED.runner_id,
            labels = EXCLUDED.labels,
            steps = EXCLUDED.steps
          RETURNING ${sql.unsafe(selectProjection)}
        `.pipe(
          Effect.flatMap((rows) =>
            rows.length === 0 ? Effect.fail(new Error("Failed to upsert job")) : toJob(rows[0])
          )
        )
      )
    )

  return {
    upsertById
  } as const
})

export class JobsStore extends Context.Tag("ci-dashboard/JobsStore")<
  JobsStore,
  {
    readonly upsertById: (input: UpsertInput) => Effect.Effect<Job>
  }
>() {}

export const Live = Layer.effect(JobsStore, makeLive)

export const upsertById = (input: UpsertInput) =>
  Effect.flatMap(JobsStore, (store) => store.upsertById(input))"}

**Effect Pattern Audit**

- `packages/server/src/config/Config.ts`: wraps `process.env` in `Schema.decode`, matching the **Define Contracts with Schema** pattern. Docs such as `content/published/define-config-schema.mdx` show the richer `Config`/`ConfigProvider` path, which would let us override values per environment and surface a tagged `ConfigError`. Recommend refactor to use the Config module plus a domain error so failures stay typed and test layers are easier.

- `packages/server/src/main.ts` & `packages/server/src/db/index.ts`: current `Layer.mergeAll` startup plus the scoped Postgres layer align with **Organize Layers into Composable Modules** (`organize-layers-into-composable-modules.mdx`) and **Compose Scoped Layers**. No change needed.

- `packages/server/src/http/server.ts` & `http/app.ts`: follow **Build a Basic HTTP Server with Effect** (`build-a-basic-http-server.mdx`) by combining `HttpServer.serveEffect`, Node layer, and contextual logging. Leave as-is; it already reflects the recommended pattern.

- `packages/server/src/logger/Logger.ts`: replaces `Logger.defaultLogger` to emit structured JSON logs, in line with the **Leveraging Structured Logging** guidance. Optional future work: add spans or log annotations from `Effect.withSpan`, but the core pattern is correct.

- `packages/server/src/db/schema/{repos,runs,jobs}.ts`: after introducing `RepositoryError`, these modules now implement **Define Contracts with Schema** and **Map Database Errors to RepositoryError** (`mapping-errors-to-fit-your-domain.mdx`). Keep the current approach.

- `packages/server/src/db/migrations.ts`: uses `Effect.tryPromise`/`Effect.forEach` to sequence filesystem and SQL work, which matches **Wrap Asynchronous Computations** (`wrap-asynchronous-computations.mdx`). What’s missing is a domain-specific `MigrationError` so checksum mismatches or IO issues stay typed. Recommend refactoring to wrap all failures with a tagged error (mirroring the repository boundary pattern).

- `packages/server/src/db/seed.ts`: now receives `RepositoryError` from the stores but still performs a raw SQL update directly. To keep the boundary consistent, consider routing that update through a helper that applies `mapRepositoryError`, or handle the error explicitly when seeding.

**Next actions**

1. Refactor config loading to use `Config`/`ConfigProvider` with a tagged error type.
2. Introduce a `MigrationError` wrapper around filesystem/SQL failures in `db/migrations.ts`.
3. Decide whether to wrap the direct SQL update in `seed.ts` with `mapRepositoryError` or keep it but handle `RepositoryError` explicitly.

{"result":"Love it. Let’s turn this into an **agent-friendly epic → story backlog** built around **Effect-TS** with **@effect/platform / @effect/platform-node** (no Hono), a **repo/org Webhook** (for events) + a **GitHub token** (for hydration/backfill). Each story is intentionally tiny (≈15–60 min), has clear DoD, inputs/outputs, and dependencies so an agent can pick up any leaf and ship.

---

# Program structure

* **Tracks** (Epics): 0–9
* Each epic has **very small stories** (S-IDs).
* Labels you can apply in your tracker: `effect`, `sql`, `api`, `sse`, `github`, `ui`, `admin`, `ops`, `tests`.

---

# Epic 0 — Repo & Runtime Foundation

**Goal:** A compilable workspace with Effect runtime, config, and logging.

**S-001** Init monorepo

* DoD: `pnpm` workspaces; packages `server`, `web`, `shared`.
* Output: root `package.json`, `tsconfig`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.
* Deps: none.

**S-002** Add Effect runtime & platform-node

* DoD: `@effect/platform`, `@effect/platform-node`, `effect`, `@effect/schema` installed; `server/src/main.ts` boots a minimal Node runtime.
* Output: `NodeRuntime.make({})` with a “hello” log.
* Deps: S-001.

**S-003** Config layer

* DoD: `Config` module using `@effect/schema` (env: `PORT`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `DATABASE_URL`, `ADMIN_KEY`).
* Output: `Config.Live` Layer exporting typed config.
* Deps: S-002.

**S-004** Logger layer

* DoD: structured JSON logger (requestId support), bound to Effect runtime.
* Output: `Logger.Live` + example log in `main.ts`.
* Deps: S-002.

**S-005** Health endpoint (platform HttpServer)

* DoD: using `@effect/platform/Http/Server` with a single `GET /healthz` returning 200 and build info.
* Output: starts server on `PORT`.
* Deps: S-003.

---

# Epic 1 — Database & Migrations

**Goal:** Postgres wired with Effect; tables and indexes created.

**S-010** SQL client layer

* DoD: `@effect/sql` (or `pg` wrapped) Layer `Db.Live` with connection pool.
* Output: `Db.sql` helper, connection tested on boot.
* Deps: S-003.

**S-011** Migration runner

* DoD: lightweight migration tool (e.g., `postgres-migrations` or custom) as an Effect service `Migrations.run()`.
* Output: `server/migrations/*.sql` processed at boot.
* Deps: S-010.

**S-012** Schema: `repos`

* DoD: SQL migration for `repos` + indexes; TypeScript model & repository.
* Output: `repos.sql`, `ReposStore` with `upsert`, `listActive`.
* Deps: S-011.

**S-013** Schema: `runs`

* DoD: `runs` table + `(repo_full_name, status, created_at)` indexes.
* Output: `runs.sql`, `RunsStore.upsert`, `RunsStore.query`.
* Deps: S-011.

**S-014** Schema: `jobs`

* DoD: `jobs` table + unique key on `github_job_id`.
* Output: `jobs.sql`, `JobsStore.upsertById`.
* Deps: S-011.

**S-015** Seed script (dev)

* DoD: a tiny seeder inserting a repo and one run for local UI testing.
* Deps: S-012..S-014.

---

# Epic 2 — GitHub Integration (Token + Webhooks)

**Goal:** Receive webhook events; hydrate details with token.

**S-020** GitHub HTTP client

* DoD: Effect service wrapping `fetch` with `Authorization: token …`, rate-limit headers logged.
* Output: `GithubClient.getJson(url)`.
* Deps: S-003, S-004.

**S-021** Webhook signature verification

* DoD: HMAC SHA-256 verify against `WEBHOOK_SECRET` (header: `X-Hub-Signature-256`).
* Output: `Webhook.verify(body, signature) -> Effect<Unit, WebhookSignatureError>`.
* Deps: S-005.

**S-022** Webhook route

* DoD: `POST /webhook/github` reading raw body (don’t pre-parse), verify, parse `X-GitHub-Event`.
* Output: 2xx ACK with idempotency (see S-023).
* Deps: S-021.

**S-023** Idempotency store

* DoD: store `delivery_id` (from `X-GitHub-Delivery`) in a tiny table or in-memory TTL map; drop duplicates.
* Output: `webhook_deliveries` table or `LRU` service.
* Deps: S-011.

**S-024** Handle `workflow_run`

* DoD: map payload → `runs` UPSERT (status, conclusion, times, html_url).
* Output: `WebhookHandlers.workflowRun(payload)`.
* Deps: S-013, S-022.

**S-025** Handle `workflow_job`

* DoD: map payload → `jobs` UPSERT.
* Output: `WebhookHandlers.workflowJob(payload)`.
* Deps: S-014, S-022.

**S-026** Repo discovery via webhook

* DoD: on event, upsert `repos` (owner/name, visibility) if unseen.

*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: packages/server/src/github/client.ts
+import { Context, Data, Effect, Layer } from "effect"
+import { Config } from "../config/Config"
+
+const GITHUB_API_VERSION = "2022-11-28"
+
+export class GithubClientRequestError extends Data.TaggedError("GithubClientRequestError")<{
+  readonly url: string
+  readonly cause: unknown
+}> {}
+
+export class GithubClientResponseError extends Data.TaggedError("GithubClientResponseError")<{
+  readonly url: string
+  readonly status: number
+  readonly body: string
+}> {}
+
+export class GithubClient extends Context.Tag("ci-dashboard/GithubClient")<
+  GithubClient,
+  {
+    readonly getJson: <A = unknown>(
+      url: string,
+      init?: Omit<RequestInit, "method">
+    ) => Effect.Effect<A, GithubClientRequestError | GithubClientResponseError>
+  }
+>() {}
+
+const parseRateLimit = (headers: Headers) => ({
+  limit: headers.get("x-ratelimit-limit") ?? "unknown",
+  remaining: headers.get("x-ratelimit-remaining") ?? "unknown",
+  reset: headers.get("x-ratelimit-reset") ?? "unknown",
+  used: headers.get("x-ratelimit-used") ?? "unknown"
+})
+
+const makeLive = Effect.gen(function* () {
+  const { githubToken } = yield* Config
+
+  const commonHeaders = {
+    Accept: "application/vnd.github+json",
+    "User-Agent": "ci-dashboard",
+    "X-GitHub-Api-Version": GITHUB_API_VERSION,
+    Authorization: `Bearer ${githubToken}`
+  } as const
+
+  const getJson = <A = unknown>(
+    url: string,
+    init?: Omit<RequestInit, "method">
+  ): Effect.Effect<A, GithubClientRequestError | GithubClientResponseError> =>
+    Effect.tryPromise({
+      try: () =>
+        fetch(url, {
+          ...init,
+          headers: {
+            ...commonHeaders,
+            ...(init?.headers instanceof Headers
+              ? Object.fromEntries(init.headers.entries())
+              : init?.headers ?? {})
+          }
+        }),
+      catch: (cause) => new GithubClientRequestError({ url, cause })
+    }).pipe(
+      Effect.flatMap((response) =>
+        Effect.gen(function* () {
+          const rateLimit = parseRateLimit(response.headers)
+          yield* Effect.logDebug("github request completed", {
+            url,
+            status: response.status,
+            rateLimit
+          })
+
+          if (!response.ok) {
+            const body = yield* Effect.tryPromise({
+              try: () => response.text(),
+              catch: () => Promise.resolve("<failed to read body>")
+            })
+            return yield* Effect.fail(
+              new GithubClientResponseError({
+                url,
+                status: response.status,
+                body
+              })
+            )
+          }
+
+          const data = (yield* Effect.tryPromise({
+            try: () => response.json() as Promise<A>,
+            catch: (cause) =>
+              Promise.reject(new GithubClientRequestError({ url, cause }))
+          })) as A
+
+          return data
+        })
+      ),
+      Effect.annotateLogs({ component: "github" })
+    )
+
+  return {
+    getJson
+  } as const
+})
+
+export const Live = Layer.effect(GithubClient, makeLive)
*** End Patch

**Adapting fetch usage and types for Node environment**

I'm figuring out how to handle fetch and related types without DOM libraries in a Node 18 context. Since TypeScript lacks DOM types like Headers and RequestInit here, I'm exploring importing their types from undici while using globalThis.fetch at runtime. To manage headers cleanly, I want to define a custom HeadersInit type as a record or array and simplify header merging by restricting to Record<string, string>. This helps me avoid complex conversions and keeps type safety when calling fetch with common headers merged. I'll also update functions to use Effect.tryPromise properly around fetch and JSON parsing. This careful juggling ensures smooth type support and runtime compatibility without adding extra dependencies.

**Error Handling Audit**

- `packages/server/src/config/Config.ts:19` wraps config failures in `AppConfigError` via `Effect.mapError`, aligning with the **Config error boundary** pattern. Keep as-is.
- `packages/server/src/db/repositoryError.ts:3` defines `RepositoryError` and helper to map DB/store failures; all repositories (`repos.ts`, `runs.ts`, `jobs.ts`) and the seeder use it, matching **Map errors to domain boundary**.
- `packages/server/src/db/migrations.ts:11` now converts IO/SQL failures to `MigrationError` with consistent logging; a `mapMigrationError` helper mirrors the repository pattern.
- `packages/server/src/db/index.ts:24` logs connection errors with `logError`; consider wrapping the failure with a `DbConnectionError` once we expose the client further, but current logging is acceptable for bootstrap.

- `packages/server/src/http` routes return JSON without explicit error surfaces yet; as we add APIs, we should follow the **Map errors to HTTP responses** pattern (e.g., `Effect.catchTag` → 4xx/5xx) to keep controllers thin.

2. Consider adding integration tests to assert error types (e.g., config failure produces `AppConfigError`) to guard these boundaries.

+import { Effect } from "effect"
+import * as HttpServerRequest from "@effect/platform/HttpServerRequest"
+import * as HttpServerResponse from "@effect/platform/HttpServerResponse"
+
+import {
+  GithubWebhookVerifier,
+  InvalidSignatureFormatError,
+  MissingSignatureError,
+  SignatureMismatchError
+} from "../../github"
+
+const SIGNATURE_HEADER = "x-hub-signature-256"
+
+const badRequest = (detail: string) =>
+  HttpServerResponse.json(
+    {
+      error: "invalid_signature_format",
+      detail
+    },
+    { status: 400 }
+  )
+
+const unauthorized = () =>
+  HttpServerResponse.json(
+    {
+      error: "missing_signature",
+      detail: `Missing ${SIGNATURE_HEADER} header`
+    },
+    { status: 401 }
+  )
+
+const forbidden = () =>
+  HttpServerResponse.json(
+    {
+      error: "signature_mismatch",
+      detail: "Signature mismatch"
+    },
+    { status: 403 }
+  )
+
+const success = () =>
+  HttpServerResponse.json(
+    {
+      status: "ok"
+    },
+    { status: 202 }
+  )
+
+const readRawBody = Effect.gen(function* () {
+  const request = yield* HttpServerRequest.HttpServerRequest
+  return yield* request.jsonBody ?? request.textBody ?? request.body
+})
+
+export const webhookRoute = Effect.gen(function* () {
+  const request = yield* HttpServerRequest.HttpServerRequest
+  const payload = yield* request.raw
+  const signature = request.headers.get(SIGNATURE_HEADER)
+
+  yield* Effect.annotateCurrentSpan({ "github.signature.present": signature != null })
+
+  const verifier = yield* GithubWebhookVerifier
+
+  const verification = yield* verifier.verify(payload, signature).pipe(
+    Effect.mapError((error) => ({ error, requestId: request.headers.get("x-github-delivery") ?? "unknown" })),
+    Effect.tapError((info) =>
+      Effect.logWarning("github webhook signature verification failed", {
+        error: info.error._tag,
+        requestId: info.requestId
+      })
+    ),
+    Effect.mapError((info) => info.error)
+  )
+
+  return yield* verification.pipe(
+    Effect.matchEffect({
+      onFailure: (error) => {
+        if (error instanceof MissingSignatureError) {
+          return unauthorized()
+        }
+
+        if (error instanceof InvalidSignatureFormatError) {
+          return badRequest(error.detail)
+        }
+
+        if (error instanceof SignatureMismatchError) {
+          return forbidden()
+        }
+
+        return HttpServerResponse.text("Unknown error", { status: 500 })
+      },
+      onSuccess: () => success()
+    })
+  )
+})

+import { Context, Effect, Layer, Schema } from "effect"
+import { SqlClient } from "@effect/sql"
+
+import { mapRepositoryError, RepositoryError, toRepositoryError } from "../repositoryError"
+
+const InsertInputSchema = Schema.Struct({
+  deliveryId: Schema.NonEmptyString,
+  event: Schema.optional(Schema.String)
+})
+
+export type InsertInput = Schema.Type<typeof InsertInputSchema>
+
+const decodeInsertInput = Schema.decodeUnknown(InsertInputSchema)
+
+const makeLive = Effect.gen(function* () {
+  const sql = yield* SqlClient.SqlClient
+
+  const markProcessed = (input: InsertInput) =>
+    decodeInsertInput(input).pipe(
+      Effect.mapError(toRepositoryError),
+      Effect.flatMap((validated) =>
+        mapRepositoryError(
+          sql<{ processed: boolean }>`
+            INSERT INTO webhook_deliveries (delivery_id, event)
+            VALUES (${validated.deliveryId}, ${validated.event ?? null})
+            ON CONFLICT (delivery_id) DO NOTHING
+            RETURNING TRUE AS processed
+          `.pipe(
+            Effect.map((rows) => rows.length > 0)
+          )
+        )
+      )
+    )
+
+  return {
+    markProcessed
+  } as const
+})
+
+export class WebhookDeliveriesStore extends Context.Tag("ci-dashboard/WebhookDeliveriesStore")<
+  WebhookDeliveriesStore,
+  {
+    readonly markProcessed: (input: InsertInput) => Effect.Effect<boolean, RepositoryError>
+  }
+>() {}
+
+export const Live = Layer.effect(WebhookDeliveriesStore, makeLive)
+
+export const markProcessed = (input: InsertInput) =>
+  Effect.flatMap(WebhookDeliveriesStore, (store) => store.markProcessed(input))
*** End Patch

TITLE: Conditionally Branch Workflows with Effect.filterOrFail
DESCRIPTION: Uses Effect.filterOrFail with named predicates to validate a user before proceeding in a workflow. This approach enhances clarity and reusability of business rules, handling potential 'DbError', 'UserIsInactive', or 'UserIsNotAdmin' errors.

SOURCE: https://github.com/pauljphilp/effectpatterns/blob/main/rules/by-use-case/core-concepts.md

LANGUAGE: typescript
CODE:
```
import { Effect } from "effect";

interface User {
  id: number;
  status: "active" | "inactive";
  roles: string[];
}

type UserError = "DbError" | "UserIsInactive" | "UserIsNotAdmin";

const findUser = (id: number): Effect.Effect<User, "DbError"> =>
  Effect.succeed({ id, status: "active", roles: ["admin"] });

// Reusable, testable predicates that document business rules.
const isActive = (user: User): boolean =>
  user.status === "active";

const isAdmin = (user: User): boolean =>
  user.roles.includes("admin");

const program = (id: number): Effect.Effect<string, UserError> =>
  findUser(id).pipe(
    // Validate user is active using Effect.filterOrFail
    Effect.filterOrFail(
      isActive,
      () => "UserIsInactive" as const
    ),
    // Validate user is admin using Effect.filterOrFail
    Effect.filterOrFail(
      isAdmin,
      () => "UserIsNotAdmin" as const
    ),
    // Success case
    Effect.map((user) => `Welcome, admin user #${user.id}!`) 
  );

// We can then handle the specific failures in a type-safe way.
const handled = program(123).pipe(
  Effect.match({
    onFailure: (error) => {
      switch (error) {
        case "UserIsNotAdmin":
          return "Access denied: requires admin role.";
        case "UserIsInactive":
          return "Access denied: user is not active.";
        case "DbError":
          return "Error: could not find user.";
        default:
          return `Unknown error: ${error}`;
      }
    },
    onSuccess: (result) => result
  })
);

// Run the program
const programWithLogging = Effect.gen(function* () {
  const result = yield* handled;
  yield* Effect.log(result);
  return result;
});

Effect.runPromise(programWithLogging);
```","type":"text"}]

+import { Context, Data, Effect, Layer } from "effect"
+
+import * as RunsStore from "../../db/schema/runs"
+import { RepositoryError } from "../../db/repositoryError"
+import { WorkflowRunPayloadSchema, WorkflowRunPayload } from "../webhookPayloads"
+
+const decodeWorkflowRunPayload = WorkflowRunPayloadSchema.pipe(
+  Effect.decodeUnknown,
+  Effect.mapError((cause) => new WorkflowRunPayloadError({ cause }))
+)
+
+export class WorkflowRunPayloadError extends Data.TaggedError("WorkflowRunPayloadError")<{
+  readonly cause: unknown
+}> {}
+
+export class WorkflowRunHandler extends Context.Tag("ci-dashboard/WorkflowRunHandler")<
+  WorkflowRunHandler,
+  {
+    readonly handle: (payload: unknown) => Effect.Effect<RunsStore.Run, RepositoryError | WorkflowRunPayloadError>
+  }
+>() {}
+
+const parseDate = (value: string | null | undefined) =>
+  value == null ? undefined : new Date(value)
+
+const mapPayloadToInput = (payload: WorkflowRunPayload): RunsStore.UpsertInput => {
+  const { workflow_run: run, repository } = payload
+
+  return {
+    repoId: run.repository_id ?? repository.id,
+    repoFullName: repository.full_name,
+    githubRunId: run.id,
+    githubRunNumber: run.run_number,
+    githubRunAttempt: run.run_attempt ?? undefined,
+    workflowName: run.workflow_name,
+    workflowId: run.workflow_id ?? undefined,
+    displayTitle: run.display_title ?? undefined,
+    event: run.event,
+    status: run.status as RunsStore.RunStatus,
+    conclusion: run.conclusion ?? undefined,
+    headBranch: run.head_branch ?? undefined,
+    headSha: run.head_sha ?? undefined,
+    htmlUrl: run.html_url ?? undefined,
+    actorLogin: run.actor?.login ?? undefined,
+    createdAt: new Date(run.created_at),
+    updatedAt: new Date(run.updated_at),
+    runStartedAt: parseDate(run.run_started_at),
+    runCompletedAt: parseDate(run.run_completed_at)
+  }
+}
+
+const makeLive = Effect.gen(function* () {
+  const handle: WorkflowRunHandler["handle"] = (payload) =>
+    Effect.gen(function* () {
+      const decoded = yield* decodeWorkflowRunPayload(payload)
+      const input = mapPayloadToInput(decoded)
+      return yield* RunsStore.upsert(input)
+    })
+
+  return { handle } as const
+})
+
+export const Live = Layer.effect(WorkflowRunHandler, makeLive)
+
+export const handleWorkflowRun = (payload: unknown) =>
+  Effect.flatMap(WorkflowRunHandler, (handler) => handler.handle(payload))
*** End Patch

payload.message:
To test Effect code idiomatically, the Effect team recommends the `@effect/vitest` helper. It bridges Vitest with the Effect runtime: you wrap your spec with `withLayer`/`layerTestEnvironment`, and each test body can be an Effect that receives the provided services. That keeps dependency wiring declarative and lets you fail with tagged errors while still reporting through Vitest.

Here’s the typical pattern:

```ts
import { describe, it, expect } from "vitest"
import { Effect } from "effect"
import { layerTestEnvironment } from "@effect/vitest"

import { MyService, MyServiceLive } from "../src/myService"

describe(
  "MyService",
  () => {
    it.effect("does something", Effect.gen(function* () {
      const svc = yield* MyService
      const result = yield* svc.doThing()
      expect(result).toEqual("ok")
    }))
  },
  // Provide whatever layers the tests need
  layerTestEnvironment(MyServiceLive)
)
```

Unfortunately, the Thought Loom sandbox blocks installing new packages (network access is restricted), so I can’t add `@effect/vitest` to this workspace right now. Once you have connectivity, install it via:

```bash
pnpm add -D @effect/vitest
```

After installing, rewrite the current tests (e.g., `webhook.test.ts`, `webhookDeliveries.test.ts`) using `it.effect` and move the layer provisioning into the `describe`’s `layerTestEnvironment` argument instead of manually calling `Effect.runPromise`. This will give you cleaner, idiomatic tests with full Effect stack traces.

**Analyzing dependency version conflicts**

I’m mapping out version mismatches between effect platform (0.72) and effect libraries (3.x), alongside vitest’s outdated version (1.6 vs 3.2). I’m considering options like aligning all effect packages to latest 3.x series or pinning older versions to avoid heavy changes, while weighing the complexity of upgrading major versions and proposing instructions to address these dependency conflicts.

payload.message:
`pnpm` is flagging peer conflicts because our Effect stack is on the older `0.7x/0.4x` line:

- `@effect/sql@0.40.14`, `@effect/platform@0.72.2`, `@effect/platform-node@0.72.1` were published before the new `@effect/experimental` split, so they expect matching peers (`@effect/platform@^0.72`, no experimental package).
- `@effect/vitest@0.26` targets the newer releases (`@effect/platform@^0.92`, `@effect/sql@^0.46`, plus `@effect/experimental`), and also requires `vitest@^3.2.0` while our workspace still has Vitest 1.x.

To resolve this you have two choices:

1. **Upgrade the entire Effect toolchain** to the latest matching versions (`effect@3.2x`, `@effect/platform@~0.92`, `@effect/sql@~0.46`, `@effect/platform-node@~0.92`, `vitest@^3.2.0`, and add `@effect/experimental`). That’s a broader dependency bump and may surface API changes to address.

2. **Stay on the current Effect versions** and skip `@effect/vitest` for now. You can continue testing by manually running effects inside Vitest (as we’ve done) until you’re ready to align all dependencies.

If the plan is to adopt the official testing helper soon, I’d recommend scheduling a dedicated upgrade pass so all Effect packages (and Vitest) sit on the same release line; otherwise we should revert the attempted `@effect/vitest` install to keep the workspace consistent.

+import { Buffer } from "node:buffer"
+import { createHmac } from "node:crypto"
+import { Effect, Layer } from "effect"
+import { expect, it, layer } from "@effect/vitest"
+
+import { Config } from "../config/Config"
+import {
+  GithubWebhookVerifier,
+  GithubWebhookVerifierLive,
+  InvalidSignatureFormatError,
+  MissingSignatureError,
+  SignatureMismatchError
+} from "./index"
+
+const SECRET = "test-secret"
+const SAMPLE_PAYLOAD = new Uint8Array(Buffer.from('{"event":"workflow_run"}', "utf8"))
+
+const configLayer = Layer.succeed(Config, {
+  port: 3000,
+  githubToken: "token",
+  webhookSecret: SECRET,
+  databaseUrl: "postgres://example",
+  adminKey: "admin"
+})
+
+const verifierLayer = Layer.provide(GithubWebhookVerifierLive, configLayer)
+
+const makeSignature = (payload: Uint8Array, secret: string) =>
+  `sha256=${createHmac("sha256", secret).update(payload).digest("hex")}`
+
+layer(verifierLayer)("GithubWebhookVerifier", (it) => {
+  it.effect("accepts a valid signature", () =>
+    Effect.gen(function* () {
+      const signature = makeSignature(SAMPLE_PAYLOAD, SECRET)
+      const verifier = yield* GithubWebhookVerifier
+      yield* verifier.verify(SAMPLE_PAYLOAD, signature)
+      expect(true).toBe(true)
+    })
+  )
+
+  it.effect("fails when signature header is missing", () =>
+    Effect.gen(function* () {
+      const verifier = yield* GithubWebhookVerifier

+      expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(MissingSignatureError)
+    })
+  )

+
+  it.effect("fails on signature mismatch", () =>

+      const signature = makeSignature(SAMPLE_PAYLOAD, "other-secret")
+      const verifier = yield* GithubWebhookVerifier
+      const error = yield* Effect.flip(verifier.verify(SAMPLE_PAYLOAD, signature))
+      expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(SignatureMismatchError)
+    })
+  )
+})

Effect’s recommended testing pattern is:

1. Define your service with `Effect.Service` (or `Context.Tag`).
2. Provide the real implementation with a Layer for production (`Foo.Live`).
3. In tests, swap that Layer with a deterministic one (often via `Layer.succeed` or a helper factory). This is the “mock layer” approach the docs emphasize.

We’re already following that pattern in our store tests: we replace the SQL client Layer with the `makeMockSqlClient` stub, then provide the store’s Live layer on top. That effectively gives us a mocked DB service.

For services like `GithubWebhookVerifier` and `WorkflowRunHandler`, we use their Live layers but pair them with deterministic dependencies (`Config`, mocked SQL client). If we need finer-grained control (e.g., simulate verifier failures), we can define lightweight mock layers:

```ts
const TestVerifier = Layer.succeed(GithubWebhookVerifier, {
  verify: () => Effect.fail(new SignatureMismatchError({ received: "bad" }))
})
```

Then, in tests, we can wrap `handleWorkflowRun` with that layer to assert behavior without going through the real implementation.

In short: yes, the Effect pattern is to use Layer-swapped mocks. We’re already doing it for DB access; we can extend the same strategy to other services by defining their interfaces with `Effect.Service`/`Context.Tag` and providing custom Layers in tests when needed.

+import { Context, Data, Effect, Layer, Schema } from "effect"
+
+import * as RunsStore from "../../db/schema/runs"
+import * as JobsStore from "../../db/schema/jobs"
+import { WorkflowJobPayloadSchema, WorkflowJobPayload } from "../webhookPayloads"
+
+const decodeWorkflowJobPayload = Schema.decodeUnknown(WorkflowJobPayloadSchema)
+
+const parseDate = (value: string | null | undefined) =>
+  value == null ? undefined : new Date(value)
+
+const toJobStep = (step: WorkflowJobPayload["workflow_job"]["steps"][number]) =>
+  ({
+    name: step.name ?? undefined,
+    status: step.status,
+    conclusion: step.conclusion ?? undefined,
+    number: step.number ?? undefined,
+    startedAt: parseDate(step.started_at),
+    completedAt: parseDate(step.completed_at)
+  }) satisfies JobsStore.JobStep
+
+export class WorkflowJobPayloadError extends Data.TaggedError("WorkflowJobPayloadError")<{
+  readonly cause: unknown
+}> {}
+
+export class WorkflowJobRunNotFoundError extends Data.TaggedError("WorkflowJobRunNotFoundError")<{
+  readonly githubRunId: number
+}> {}
+
+export class WorkflowJobHandler extends Context.Tag("ci-dashboard/WorkflowJobHandler")<
+  WorkflowJobHandler,
+  {
+    readonly handle: (
+      payload: unknown
+    ) => Effect.Effect<JobsStore.Job, WorkflowJobPayloadError | WorkflowJobRunNotFoundError | JobsStore.RepositoryError>
+  }
+>() {}
+
+const makeLive = Effect.gen(function* () {
+  const handle: WorkflowJobHandler["handle"] = (payload) =>
+    Effect.gen(function* () {
+      const decoded = yield* decodeWorkflowJobPayload(payload).pipe(
+        Effect.mapError((cause) => new WorkflowJobPayloadError({ cause }))
+      )
+
+      const { workflow_job: job } = decoded
+
+      const existingRun = yield* RunsStore.findByGithubRunId(job.run_id)
+
+      if (!existingRun) {
+        return yield* Effect.fail(
+          new WorkflowJobRunNotFoundError({
+            githubRunId: job.run_id
+          })
+        )
+      }
+
+      const mapping: JobsStore.UpsertInput = {
+        runId: existingRun.id,
+        githubJobId: job.id,
+        githubRunId: job.run_id,
+        githubRunAttempt: job.run_attempt ?? undefined,
+        name: job.name,
+        status: job.status,
+        conclusion: job.conclusion ?? undefined,
+        startedAt: parseDate(job.started_at),
+        completedAt: parseDate(job.completed_at),
+        queuedAt: parseDate(job.queued_at),
+        htmlUrl: job.html_url ?? undefined,
+        checkRunUrl: job.check_run_url ?? undefined,
+        runnerName: job.runner_name ?? undefined,
+        runnerGroup: job.runner_group ?? undefined,
+        runnerId: job.runner_id ?? undefined,
+        labels: job.labels ?? [],
+        steps: job.steps?.map(toJobStep)
+      }
+
+      return yield* JobsStore.upsertById(mapping)
+    })
+
+  return { handle } as const
+})
+
+export const Live = Layer.effect(WorkflowJobHandler, makeLive)
+
+export const handleWorkflowJob = (payload: unknown) =>

  id: Schema.Number,
  githubRepoId: Schema.optional(Schema.Number),
  owner: Schema.NonEmptyString,
  name: Schema.NonEmptyString,
  fullName: Schema.NonEmptyString,
  visibility: RepoVisibilitySchema,
  isActive: Schema.Boolean,
  backfilledAt: Schema.optional(Schema.Date),
  createdAt: Schema.Date,
  updatedAt: Schema.Date
})

export type Repo = Schema.Type<typeof RepoSchema>

const UpsertInputSchema = Schema.Struct({
  owner: Schema.NonEmptyString,
  name: Schema.NonEmptyString,
  visibility: RepoVisibilitySchema,
  githubRepoId: Schema.optional(Schema.Number)
})

export type UpsertInput = Schema.Type<typeof UpsertInputSchema>

interface RepoRow {
  readonly id: number | string
  readonly githubRepoId: number | string | null
  readonly owner: string
  readonly name: string
  readonly fullName: string
  readonly visibility: RepoVisibility
  readonly isActive: boolean
  readonly backfilledAt: string | Date | null
  readonly createdAt: string | Date
  readonly updatedAt: string | Date
}

const decodeRepo = Schema.decodeUnknown(RepoSchema)
const decodeUpsertInput = Schema.decodeUnknown(UpsertInputSchema)

const toRepo = (row: RepoRow) =>
  decodeRepo({
    id: typeof row.id === "string" ? Number.parseInt(row.id, 10) : row.id,
    githubRepoId:
      row.githubRepoId === null
        ? undefined
        : typeof row.githubRepoId === "string"
          ? Number.parseInt(row.githubRepoId, 10)
          : row.githubRepoId,
    owner: row.owner,
    name: row.name,
    fullName: row.fullName,
    visibility: row.visibility,
    isActive: row.isActive,
    backfilledAt:
      row.backfilledAt === null
        ? undefined
        : row.backfilledAt instanceof Date
          ? row.backfilledAt
          : new Date(row.backfilledAt),
    createdAt: row.createdAt instanceof Date ? row.createdAt : new Date(row.createdAt),
    updatedAt: row.updatedAt instanceof Date ? row.updatedAt : new Date(row.updatedAt)
  }).pipe(Effect.mapError(toRepositoryError))

const selectProjection = `
  id,
  github_repo_id AS "githubRepoId",
  owner,
  name,
  full_name AS "fullName",
  visibility,
  is_active AS "isActive",
  backfilled_at AS "backfilledAt",
  created_at AS "createdAt",
  updated_at AS "updatedAt"
`

const makeLive = Effect.gen(function* () {
  const sql = yield* SqlClient.SqlClient

  const upsert = (input: UpsertInput) =>
    decodeUpsertInput(input).pipe(
      Effect.mapError(toRepositoryError),
      Effect.flatMap((validated) =>
        mapRepositoryError(
          sql<RepoRow>`
          INSERT INTO repos (github_repo_id, owner, name, visibility)
          VALUES (${validated.githubRepoId ?? null}, ${validated.owner}, ${validated.name}, ${validated.visibility})
          ON CONFLICT (owner, name) DO UPDATE SET
            github_repo_id = EXCLUDED.github_repo_id,
            visibility = EXCLUDED.visibility
          RETURNING ${sql.unsafe(selectProjection)}
        `).pipe(
          Effect.flatMap((rows) =>
            rows.length === 0
              ? Effect.fail(toRepositoryError(new Error("Failed to upsert repo")))
              : toRepo(rows[0])
          )
        )
      )
    )

  const listActive = mapRepositoryError(
    sql<RepoRow>`
    SELECT ${sql.unsafe(selectProjection)}
    FROM repos
    WHERE is_active = TRUE
    ORDER BY owner, name
  `.pipe(
      Effect.flatMap((rows) => Effect.forEach(rows, toRepo, { concurrency: 1 })),
      Effect.map((rows) => rows as ReadonlyArray<Repo>)
    )
  )"}

+import * as HttpServerResponse from "@effect/platform/HttpServerResponse"
+
+import runPayload from "../../../test/fixtures/github/workflow_run.json"
+import jobPayload from "../../../test/fixtures/github/workflow_job.json"
+import { Config } from "../../config/Config"
+import {
+  GithubWebhookVerifierLive,
+  WorkflowJobHandler,
+  WorkflowRunHandler,
+  handleWorkflowJob,
+  handleWorkflowRun
+} from "../../github"
+import { WebhookDeliveriesStore } from "../../db/schema/webhookDeliveries"
+import * as RunsStore from "../../db/schema/runs"
+import * as JobsStore from "../../db/schema/jobs"
+import { webhookRoute } from "./webhook"
+
+const SECRET = "test-secret"
+
+const signPayload = (body: string) =>
+  `sha256=${createHmac("sha256", SECRET).update(body).digest("hex")}`
+
+const makeRequest = (body: string, event: string, deliveryId: string, signature: string) => {
+  const buffer = Buffer.from(body)
+  const headerMap = new Map<string, string>([
+    ["content-type", "application/json"],
+    ["x-github-event", event],
+    ["x-github-delivery", deliveryId],
+    ["x-hub-signature-256", signature]
+  ])
+
+  const headers = {
+    get: (name: string) => headerMap.get(name.toLowerCase()) ?? null
+  }
+
+  return {
+    method: "POST",
+    url: "http://localhost/webhook/github",
+    originalUrl: "/webhook/github",
+    headers,
+    arrayBuffer: Effect.succeed(buffer.buffer),
+    json: Effect.sync(() => JSON.parse(body)),
+    text: Effect.succeed(body)
+  } as HttpServerRequest.HttpServerRequest
+}
+
+const configLayer = Layer.succeed(Config, {
+  port: 3000,
+  githubToken: "token",
+  webhookSecret: SECRET,
+  databaseUrl: "postgres://example",
+  adminKey: "admin"
+})
+
+const deliveriesLayer = Layer.effect(
+  WebhookDeliveriesStore,
+  Effect.sync(() => {
+    const seen = new Set<string>()
+    return {
+      markProcessed: ({ deliveryId }: { deliveryId: string }) =>
+        Effect.sync(() => {
+          const isNew = !seen.has(deliveryId)
+          if (isNew) {
+            seen.add(deliveryId)
+          }
+          return isNew
+        })
+    }
+  })
+)
+
+const handledRuns: Array<unknown> = []
+const handledJobs: Array<unknown> = []
+
+const workflowRunHandlerLayer = Layer.succeed(
+  WorkflowRunHandler,
+  {
+    handle: (payload: unknown) => {
+      handledRuns.push(payload)
+      const run: RunsStore.Run = {
+        id: 42,
+        repoId: 7,
+        repoFullName: "demo/ci-dashboard",
+        githubRunId: runPayload.workflow_run.id,
+        githubRunNumber: runPayload.workflow_run.run_number,
+        githubRunAttempt: runPayload.workflow_run.run_attempt ?? undefined,
+        workflowName: runPayload.workflow_run.workflow_name,
+        workflowId: runPayload.workflow_run.workflow_id ?? undefined,
+        displayTitle: runPayload.workflow_run.display_title ?? undefined,
+        event: runPayload.workflow_run.event,
+        status: runPayload.workflow_run.status as RunsStore.RunStatus,
+        conclusion: runPayload.workflow_run.conclusion ?? undefined,
+        headBranch: runPayload.workflow_run.head_branch ?? undefined,
+        headSha: runPayload.workflow_run.head_sha ?? undefined,
+        htmlUrl: runPayload.workflow_run.html_url ?? undefined,
+        actorLogin: runPayload.workflow_run.actor?.login ?? undefined,
+        createdAt: new Date(runPayload.workflow_run.created_at),
+        updatedAt: new Date(runPayload.workflow_run.updated_at),
+        runStartedAt: runPayload.workflow_run.run_started_at
+          ? new Date(runPayload.workflow_run.run_started_at)
+          : undefined,
+        runCompletedAt: runPayload.workflow_run.run_completed_at
+          ? new Date(runPayload.workflow_run.run_completed_at)
+          : undefined,
+        ingestedAt: new Date(),
+        ingestedUpdatedAt: new Date()
+      }
+      return Effect.succeed(run)
+    }
+  }
+)
+
+const workflowJobHandlerLayer = Layer.succeed(
+  WorkflowJobHandler,
+  {
+    handle: (payload: unknown) => {
+      handledJobs.push(payload)
+      const job: JobsStore.Job = {
+        id: 99,
+        runId: 42,
+        githubJobId: jobPayload.workflow_job.id,
+        githubRunId: jobPayload.workflow_job.run_id,
+        githubRunAttempt: jobPayload.workflow_job.run_attempt ?? undefined,
+        name: jobPayload.workflow_job.name,
+        status: jobPayload.workflow_job.status as JobsStore.JobStatus,
+        conclusion: jobPayload.workflow_job.conclusion ?? undefined,
+        startedAt: jobPayload.workflow_job.started_at
+          ? new Date(jobPayload.workflow_job.started_at)
+          : undefined,
+        completedAt: jobPayload.workflow_job.completed_at
+          ? new Date(jobPayload.workflow_job.completed_at)
+          : undefined,
+        queuedAt: jobPayload.workflow_job.queued_at
+          ? new Date(jobPayload.workflow_job.queued_at)
+          : undefined,
+        htmlUrl: jobPayload.workflow_job.html_url ?? undefined,
+        checkRunUrl: jobPayload.workflow_job.check_run_url ?? undefined,
+        runnerName: jobPayload.workflow_job.runner_name ?? undefined,
+        runnerGroup: jobPayload.workflow_job.runner_group ?? undefined,
+        runnerId: jobPayload.workflow_job.runner_id ?? undefined,
+        labels: jobPayload.workflow_job.labels ?? [],
+        steps: [],
+        createdAt: new Date(),
+        updatedAt: new Date()
+      }
+      return Effect.succeed(job)
+    }
+  }
+)
+
+const baseLayer = Layer.mergeAll(
+  configLayer,
+  GithubWebhookVerifierLive,
+  deliveriesLayer,
+  workflowRunHandlerLayer,
+  workflowJobHandlerLayer
+)
+
+const executeRoute = (request: HttpServerRequest.HttpServerRequest) =>
+  Effect.provide(
+    webhookRoute,
+    Layer.mergeAll(baseLayer, Layer.succeed(HttpServerRequest.HttpServerRequest, request))
+  )
+
+const readJson = (response: HttpServerResponse.HttpServerResponse) =>
+  Effect.gen(function* () {
+    const webResponse = yield* HttpServerResponse.toWeb(response)
+    return yield* Effect.tryPromise(() => webResponse.json())
+  })
+
+it.effect("processes run and job webhook events end-to-end", () =>
+  Effect.gen(function* () {
+    const runBody = JSON.stringify(runPayload)
+    const runRequest = makeRequest(runBody, "workflow_run", "delivery-run", signPayload(runBody))
+
+    const runResponse = yield* executeRoute(runRequest)
+    const runJson = yield* readJson(runResponse)
+
+    expect(runJson.status).toBe("accepted")
+    expect(handledRuns).toHaveLength(1)
+
+    // Duplicate delivery should be ignored
+    const duplicateResponse = yield* executeRoute(runRequest)
+    const duplicateJson = yield* readJson(duplicateResponse)
+    expect(duplicateJson.status).toBe("duplicate")
+
+    const jobBody = JSON.stringify(jobPayload)
+    const jobRequest = makeRequest(jobBody, "workflow_job", "delivery-job", signPayload(jobBody))
+
+    const jobResponse = yield* executeRoute(jobRequest)
+    const jobJson = yield* readJson(jobResponse)
+
+    expect(jobJson.status).toBe("accepted")
+    expect(handledJobs).toHaveLength(1)
+  })
+)
*** End Patch

**Workflow Job Pipeline**

- Route now dispatches `workflow_job` events, surfaces detailed JSON errors, and logs missing-run cases while returning 202 for ignored jobs (`packages/server/src/http/routes/webhook.ts`).

{"output":"Love it. Let’s turn this into an **agent-friendly epic → story backlog** built around **Effect-TS** with **@effect/platform / @effect/platform-node** (no Hono), a **repo/org Webhook** (for events) + a **GitHub token** (for hydration/backfill). Each story is intentionally tiny (≈15–60 min), has clear DoD, inputs/outputs, and dependencies so an agent can pick up any leaf and ship.

---

# Program structure

* **Tracks** (Epics): 0–9
* Each epic has **very small stories** (S-IDs).
* Labels you can apply in your tracker: `effect`, `sql`, `api`, `sse`, `github`, `ui`, `admin`, `ops`, `tests`.

---

# Epic 0 — Repo & Runtime Foundation

**Goal:** A compilable workspace with Effect runtime, config, and logging.

**S-001** Init monorepo

* DoD: `pnpm` workspaces; packages `server`, `web`, `shared`.
* Output: root `package.json`, `tsconfig`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.
* Deps: none.

**S-002** Add Effect runtime & platform-node

* DoD: `@effect/platform`, `@effect/platform-node`, `effect`, `@effect/schema` installed; `server/src/main.ts` boots a minimal Node runtime.
* Output: `NodeRuntime.make({})` with a “hello” log.
* Deps: S-001.

**S-003** Config layer

* DoD: `Config` module using `@effect/schema` (env: `PORT`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `DATABASE_URL`, `ADMIN_KEY`).
* Output: `Config.Live` Layer exporting typed config.
* Deps: S-002.

**S-004** Logger layer

* DoD: structured JSON logger (requestId support), bound to Effect runtime.
* Output: `Logger.Live` + example log in `main.ts`.
* Deps: S-002.

**S-005** Health endpoint (platform HttpServer)

* DoD: using `@effect/platform/Http/Server` with a single `GET /healthz` returning 200 and build info.
* Output: starts server on `PORT`.
* Deps: S-003.

---

# Epic 1 — Database & Migrations

**Goal:** Postgres wired with Effect; tables and indexes created.

**S-010** SQL client layer

* DoD: `@effect/sql` (or `pg` wrapped) Layer `Db.Live` with connection pool.
* Output: `Db.sql` helper, connection tested on boot.
* Deps: S-003.

**S-011** Migration runner

* DoD: lightweight migration tool (e.g., `postgres-migrations` or custom) as an Effect service `Migrations.run()`.
* Output: `server/migrations/*.sql` processed at boot.
* Deps: S-010.

**S-012** Schema: `repos`

* DoD: SQL migration for `repos` + indexes; TypeScript model & repository.
* Output: `repos.sql`, `ReposStore` with `upsert`, `listActive`.
* Deps: S-011.

**S-013** Schema: `runs`

* DoD: `runs` table + `(repo_full_name, status, created_at)` indexes.
* Output: `runs.sql`, `RunsStore.upsert`, `RunsStore.query`.
* Deps: S-011.

**S-014** Schema: `jobs`

* DoD: `jobs` table + unique key on `github_job_id`.
* Output: `jobs.sql`, `JobsStore.upsertById`.
* Deps: S-011.

**S-015** Seed script (dev)

* DoD: a tiny seeder inserting a repo and one run for local UI testing.
* Deps: S-012..S-014.

---

# Epic 2 — GitHub Integration (Token + Webhooks)

**Goal:** Receive webhook events; hydrate details with token.

**S-020** GitHub HTTP client

* DoD: Effect service wrapping `fetch` with `Authorization: token …`, rate-limit headers logged.
* Output: `GithubClient.getJson(url)`.
* Deps: S-003, S-004.

**S-021** Webhook signature verification

* DoD: HMAC SHA-256 verify against `WEBHOOK_SECRET` (header: `X-Hub-Signature-256`).
* Output: `Webhook.verify(body, signature) -> Effect<Unit, WebhookSignatureError>`.
* Deps: S-005.

**S-022** Webhook route

* DoD: `POST /webhook/github` reading raw body (don’t pre-parse), verify, parse `X-GitHub-Event`.
* Output: 2xx ACK with idempotency (see S-023).
* Deps: S-021.

**S-023** Idempotency store

* DoD: store `delivery_id` (from `X-GitHub-Delivery`) in a tiny table or in-memory TTL map; drop duplicates.
* Output: `webhook_deliveries` table or `LRU` service.
* Deps: S-011.

**S-024** Handle `workflow_run`

* DoD: map payload → `runs` UPSERT (status, conclusion, times, html_url).
* Output: `WebhookHandlers.workflowRun(payload)`.
* Deps: S-013, S-022.

**S-025** Handle `workflow_job`

* DoD: map payload → `jobs` UPSERT.
* Output: `WebhookHandlers.workflowJob(payload)`.
* Deps: S-014, S-022.

**S-026** Repo discovery via webhook

* DoD: on event, upsert `repos` (owner/name, visibility) if unseen.
* Output: ensures dashboards work without manual pre-seed.
* Deps: S-012, S-024/S-025.

**S-027** Dev tunnel wiring

* DoD: smee/ngrok URL configurable; docs + script to register a repo/org webhook with secret.
* Output: `docs/webhook-dev.md`, `scripts/register-webhook.ts`.
* Deps: S-020.

---

# Epic 3 — Hydration, Backfill & Reconcile

**Goal:** Fill missing details, initial history, and handle misses.

**S-030** Hydrate jobs for a run

* DoD: `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{run_id}/jobs`, store all jobs.

I see the issue is that the store resets on each request because the layer recreates the state, so duplicate deliveries aren't detected properly. This should fix the repeated 202 responses for duplicates.

*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: packages/server/scripts/register-webhook.ts
+import { Effect, Layer, Config as ConfigModule, ConfigProvider, Data } from "effect"
+import { runMain } from "@effect/platform-node/NodeRuntime"
+import { fetch } from "undici"
+
+import { Config, Live as ConfigLive } from "../src/config/Config"
+import { GithubClientRequestError } from "../src/github"
+import { Live as LoggerLive, withRequestId } from "../src/logger/Logger"
+
+const envProviderLayer = Layer.succeed(
+  ConfigProvider.ConfigProvider,
+  ConfigProvider.fromEnv()
+)
+
+const registrationConfig = ConfigModule.all({
+  target: ConfigModule.nonEmptyString("GITHUB_WEBHOOK_TARGET"),
+  tunnelUrl: ConfigModule.nonEmptyString("WEBHOOK_TUNNEL_URL"),
+  events: ConfigModule.optional(ConfigModule.nonEmptyString("GITHUB_WEBHOOK_EVENTS"))
+}).pipe(
+  ConfigModule.withDescription(
+    "Webhook registration configuration. Set GITHUB_WEBHOOK_TARGET to repo:<owner>/<repo>, org:<org>, or <owner>/<repo>."
+  ),
+  Effect.provideLayer(envProviderLayer)
+)
+
+class GithubWebhookRegistrationError extends Data.TaggedError("GithubWebhookRegistrationError")<{
+  readonly status: number
+  readonly body: string
+}> {}
+
+type WebhookTarget =
+  | { readonly type: "repo"; readonly owner: string; readonly name: string }
+  | { readonly type: "org"; readonly org: string }
+
+const parseTarget = (target: string): WebhookTarget => {
+  const normalized = target.trim()
+  if (normalized.length === 0) {
+    throw new Error("GITHUB_WEBHOOK_TARGET cannot be empty")
+  }
+
+  if (normalized.startsWith("org:")) {
+    const org = normalized.slice(4).trim()
+    if (org.length === 0) {
+      throw new Error("GITHUB_WEBHOOK_TARGET org: value is missing an organization name")
+    }
+    return { type: "org", org }
+  }
+
+  const repoValue = normalized.startsWith("repo:") ? normalized.slice(5) : normalized
+  const [owner, name] = repoValue.split("/", 2)
+  if (!owner || !name) {
+    throw new Error(
+      "GITHUB_WEBHOOK_TARGET must be repo:<owner>/<repo>, org:<org>, or <owner>/<repo>"
+    )
+  }
+  return { type: "repo", owner, name }
+}
+
+const appendWebhookPath = (base: string) => {
+  const url = new URL(base.endsWith("/") ? base : `${base}/`)
+  url.pathname = `${url.pathname.replace(/\/+$/, "")}/webhook/github`
+  return url.toString()
+}
+
+const parseEvents = (events: string | undefined) =>
+  events ? events.split(",").map((event) => event.trim()).filter((event) => event.length > 0) : undefined
+
+const runtimeLayer = Layer.mergeAll(ConfigLive, LoggerLive)
+
+const program = Effect.gen(function* () {
+  const [{ target, tunnelUrl, events: eventsEnv }, { githubToken, webhookSecret }] = yield* Effect.all([
+    registrationConfig,
+    Config
+  ])
+
+  const parsedTarget = parseTarget(target)
+  const hookEvents = parseEvents(eventsEnv) ?? ["workflow_run", "workflow_job"]
+  const deliveryUrl = appendWebhookPath(tunnelUrl)
+
+  yield* Effect.logInfo("registering webhook", {
+    target: parsedTarget.type === "repo" ? `${parsedTarget.owner}/${parsedTarget.name}` : parsedTarget.org,
+    scope: parsedTarget.type,
+    deliveryUrl,
+    events: hookEvents
+  })
+
+  const endpoint =
+    parsedTarget.type === "repo"
+      ? `https://api.github.com/repos/${parsedTarget.owner}/${parsedTarget.name}/hooks`
+      : `https://api.github.com/orgs/${parsedTarget.org}/hooks`
+
+  const response = yield* Effect.tryPromise({
+    try: () =>
+      fetch(endpoint, {
+        method: "POST",
+        headers: {
+          Accept: "application/vnd.github+json",
+          Authorization: `Bearer ${githubToken}`,
+          "X-GitHub-Api-Version": "2022-11-28",
+          "Content-Type": "application/json"
+        },
+        body: JSON.stringify({
+          name: "web",
+          active: true,
+          events: hookEvents,
+          config: {
+            url: deliveryUrl,
+            content_type: "json",
+            secret: webhookSecret,
+            insecure_ssl: "0"
+          }
+        })
+      }),
+    catch: (cause) => new GithubClientRequestError({ url: endpoint, cause })
+  })
+
+  if (!response.ok) {
+    const body = yield* Effect.tryPromise({
+      try: () => response.text(),
+      catch: (cause) => cause
+    }).pipe(Effect.orElseSucceed(() => "<failed to read body>"))
+
+    return yield* Effect.fail(
+      new GithubWebhookRegistrationError({
+        status: response.status,
+        body
+      })
+    )
+  }
+
+  const result = yield* Effect.tryPromise({
+    try: () => response.json() as Promise<Record<string, unknown>>,
+    catch: (cause) => cause
+  })
+
+  yield* Effect.logInfo("webhook registered", {
+    id: result.id,
+    url: result.url,
+    test_url: result.test_url
+  })
+}).pipe(
+  Effect.provideLayer(runtimeLayer),
+  withRequestId("register-webhook"),
+  Effect.tapErrorTag("GithubWebhookRegistrationError", (error) =>
+    Effect.logError("github webhook registration failed", {
+      status: error.status,
+      body: error.body
+    })
+  )
+)
+
+runMain(program)
*** End Patch

*** Add File: docs/webhook-dev.md
+# GitHub Webhook Development Setup
+
+When developing against GitHub Actions webhooks locally you need a tunnel so
+GitHub can reach your workstation, plus a webhook registration that points at
+that tunnel. This guide walks through the happy path using either
+[smee](https://smee.io/) or [ngrok](https://ngrok.com/).
+
+## 1. Start a tunnel
+
+Expose your local webhook endpoint (`http://localhost:3000/webhook/github`) with
+one of the following:
+
+- **smee** – create a channel via the web UI or `npx smee-client`, and forward to
+  `http://localhost:3000/webhook/github`.
+- **ngrok** – `ngrok http 3000` and note the generated HTTPS URL.
+
+Keep the tunnel process running while you work.
+
+## 2. Configure environment variables
+
+The repository already expects the standard configuration variables documented
+in `packages/server/src/config/Config.ts` (e.g. `GITHUB_TOKEN`,
+`WEBHOOK_SECRET`). For webhook registration add:
+
+| Variable | Required | Description |
+| -------- | -------- | ----------- |
+| `WEBHOOK_TUNNEL_URL` | ✅ | Public tunnel base URL (e.g. `https://abc123.ngrok.app`). The script appends `/webhook/github`. |
+| `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_TARGET` | ✅ | Where to register the webhook. Use `repo:<owner>/<repo>`, `<owner>/<repo>`, or `org:<org-name>`. |
+| `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_EVENTS` | optional | Comma-separated list of events. Defaults to `workflow_run,workflow_job`. |
+
+Example `.env` snippet:
+
+```bash
+GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_yourtoken
+WEBHOOK_SECRET=dev-secret
+WEBHOOK_TUNNEL_URL=https://abc123.ngrok.app
+GITHUB_WEBHOOK_TARGET=repo:my-org/my-repo
+```
+
+## 3. Register the webhook
+
+Run the Effect-based helper from the server workspace:
+
+```bash
+pnpm --filter @ci-dashboard/server register-webhook
+```
+
+The command will log the resolved target, events, and the hook metadata (GitHub
+ID, URL, test URL). If the GitHub API reports a validation error (e.g. webhook
+already exists or token lacks scopes) the script logs the response body to
+help you debug.
+
+## 4. Test the webhook
+
+Use GitHub's “Redeliver” button or the `test_url` emitted by the script to send
+a payload. Keep your tunnel running while you iterate on webhook handlers.
*** End Patch

+import { Schema } from "effect"
+
+import type * as JobsStore from "../db/schema/jobs"
+
+const JobLabelSchema = Schema.Array(Schema.String)
+
+const WorkflowJobStepSchema = Schema.Struct({
+  name: Schema.optional(Schema.String),
+  status: Schema.NonEmptyString,
+  conclusion: Schema.optional(Schema.String),
+  number: Schema.optional(Schema.Number),
+  started_at: Schema.optional(Schema.String),
+  completed_at: Schema.optional(Schema.String)
+})
+
+const WorkflowJobSchema = Schema.Struct({
+  id: Schema.Number,
+  run_id: Schema.Number,
+  run_attempt: Schema.optional(Schema.Number),
+  name: Schema.NonEmptyString,
+  status: Schema.NonEmptyString,
+  conclusion: Schema.optional(Schema.String),
+  started_at: Schema.optional(Schema.String),
+  completed_at: Schema.optional(Schema.String),
+  queued_at: Schema.optional(Schema.String),
+  html_url: Schema.optional(Schema.String),
+  check_run_url: Schema.optional(Schema.String),
+  runner_name: Schema.optional(Schema.String),
+  runner_group: Schema.optional(Schema.String),
+  runner_id: Schema.optional(Schema.Number),
+  labels: Schema.optional(JobLabelSchema),
+  steps: Schema.optional(Schema.Array(WorkflowJobStepSchema))
+})
+
+export type GithubWorkflowJob = Schema.Type<typeof WorkflowJobSchema>
+export type GithubWorkflowJobStep = Schema.Type<typeof WorkflowJobStepSchema>
+
+const parseDate = (value: string | null | undefined) =>
+  value == null ? undefined : new Date(value)
+
+const toJobStep = (step: GithubWorkflowJobStep) =>
+  ({
+    name: step.name ?? undefined,
+    status: step.status,
+    conclusion: step.conclusion ?? undefined,
+    number: step.number ?? undefined,
+    startedAt: parseDate(step.started_at),
+    completedAt: parseDate(step.completed_at)
+  }) satisfies JobsStore.JobStep
+
+export const mapJobToUpsertInput = (
+  job: GithubWorkflowJob,
+  runId: number
+): JobsStore.UpsertInput => ({
+  runId,
+  githubJobId: job.id,
+  githubRunId: job.run_id,
+  githubRunAttempt: job.run_attempt ?? undefined,
+  name: job.name,
+  status: job.status as JobsStore.JobStatus,
+  conclusion: job.conclusion ?? undefined,
+  startedAt: parseDate(job.started_at),
+  completedAt: parseDate(job.completed_at),
+  queuedAt: parseDate(job.queued_at),
+  htmlUrl: job.html_url ?? undefined,
+  checkRunUrl: job.check_run_url ?? undefined,
+  runnerName: job.runner_name ?? undefined,
+  runnerGroup: job.runner_group ?? undefined,
+  runnerId: job.runner_id ?? undefined,
+  labels: job.labels ?? [],
+  steps: job.steps?.map(toJobStep)
+})
